concept: A directed graph is a set of nodes (vertices) connected by edges that only go one way.
If there's an edge from A to B, that doesn't automatically mean there's a path from B back to A — direction matters and must be tracked explicitly.

Representing this as an adjacency list — each vertex holding a list of the vertices it points to — takes O(V + E) space and is the standard choice for sparse graphs; the alternative, an adjacency matrix, takes O(V²) regardless of how many edges actually exist, which wastes space fast once a graph has many more vertices than edges.
1.analogy: A city's one-way streets. Being able to drive from the library to the park doesn't guarantee you can drive straight back the same way — you might need an entirely different route home.
1.mascotDialogue: An arrow in a directed graph means exactly one thing: you can go this way. It says nothing at all about whether you can come back.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8 sets exactly one cell in the matrix. A directed edge only ever writes adjacency[u][v] — never touches adjacency[v][u].

3.mascotDialogue: Every arrowhead points one way. This particular loop happens to form a cycle, but notice each edge is still individually one-directional.

4.bugDescription: Some downstream code assumed that adding edge 0->1 implicitly also created edge 1->0, as if this were an undirected graph. It doesn't — adjacency[1][0] remains 0, and any traversal starting from vertex 1 will never reach vertex 0 through this edge.
4.mascotDialogue: This is the single most common directed-graph mistake: treating a one-way arrow like it secretly goes both ways. It doesn't, and the visual only ever draws the direction you actually set.

5.question: If addDirectedEdge(g, 3, 7) is called and nothing else, what does g.adjacency[7][3] equal?
hints: A directed edge only writes one cell of the adjacency matrix.
The reverse direction is a completely separate edge that must be added explicitly.
5.solution: It remains 0 — a directed edge from 3 to 7 only sets adjacency[3][7]; the reverse edge 7->3 does not exist unless added as its own, separate call.
